function.name: get_dominant_trait
function.description: Calculate the dominant genetic trait of an organism based on its genetic makeup. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

allele1.description: The first allele of the organism.

allele2.description: The second allele of the organism.

inheritance_pattern.description: The type of inheritance pattern (could be dominant, recessive, or co-dominant). Default is 'dominant'.

message.content:
**rs7412 (APOE ε2 allele) – allele frequency in European populations**

| Population group | Minor allele (C) frequency | Major allele (T) frequency |
|------------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Non‑Finnish Europeans (gnomAD v2.1.1) | **≈ 0.12–0.13** (12–13 %) | ≈ 0.87–0.88 (87–88 %) |
| 1000 Genomes Phase 3 – CEU (Utah residents with Northern/Western European ancestry) | ≈ 0.11 (11 %) | ≈ 0.89 (89 %) |
| 1000 Genomes Phase 3 – TSI (Toscani in Italy) | ≈ 0.14 (14 %) | ≈ 0.86 (86 %) |
| 1000 Genomes Phase 3 – GBR (British in England and Scotland) | ≈ 0.10 (10 %) | ≈ 0.90 (90 %) |

**Key points**

1. **rs7412 is the APOE ε2 allele** – the “C” allele at position 19,292,385 on chromosome 19 (GRCh37/hg19).  
2. The allele frequency varies slightly among European sub‑populations but generally falls in the 10–15 % range.  
3. These figures come from large public datasets (gnomAD v2.1.1 and 1000 Genomes Phase 3).  
4. The frequency is expressed as the proportion of all alleles in the sample; for a diploid genome, this corresponds to roughly 5–7 % of individuals being homozygous for the C allele (ε2/ε2) and ~25–30 % heterozygous (ε2/ε3 or ε2/ε4).

**Reference sources**

- gnomAD v2.1.1 (non‑Finnish Europeans): https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/
- 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3: https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal

These numbers are estimates based on current reference panels and may shift slightly with newer releases or more fine‑grained sub‑population analyses.
